easy.def: Able to wait without getting upset.
examples: Be patient. It will be your turn soon.
The patient dog waited for its food.
Be patient while the cake bakes.

more.def: Able to stay calm while waiting or when something is hard.
examples: The patient teacher explained the problem again until everyone understood.
You must be patient when you are fishing.
She is patient with her little brother when he learns new games.

easy.def: Shapes, colors, or things that repeat again and again.
examples: My shirt has a pattern of red and blue dots.
The rug has a pattern of stars.
Clap the pattern with me.

more.def: A design or set of things that repeats in a regular way.
examples: Can you find the pattern in these numbers: 2, 4, 6, 8?
The tiles made a pattern of blue and white squares.
Scientists look for patterns in the weather.
The garden is a peaceful place.
The baby looks peaceful when asleep.
We had a peaceful day at the lake.

more.def: Quiet and calm; without fighting or trouble.
examples: It was a peaceful morning with no sound but the birds.
The two countries found a peaceful way to solve their problem.
The village is peaceful at night.
That is a peculiar hat!
The soup has a peculiar taste.
My cat makes a peculiar sound.

more.def: Strange or unusual in a way that makes you notice.
examples: There was a peculiar smell coming from the science room.
It was peculiar that the shop was closed on a Monday.
The bird had a peculiar way of hopping sideways.

easy.def: When someone says it is okay to do something.
examples: I have permission to go outside.
Ask for permission first.
Dad gave me permission to ride my bike.

more.def: An okay from someone that allows you to do something.
examples: You need a parent's permission to go on the field trip.
The pilot waited for permission to land.
She asked permission to borrow her sister's sweater.

easy.def: A big, round thing in space that goes around a star.
examples: Earth is the planet we live on.
Mars is a red planet.
Our planet has land and sea.

more.def: A large, round object in space that travels around a star such as the sun.
examples: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
Saturn is the planet with bright rings.
We must take care of our planet.
It is polite to say "thank you."
The polite girl said "please."
Be polite to the bus driver.

more.def: Having good manners and showing respect for other people.
examples: The polite boy held the door open for everyone.
It is polite to wait until everyone is served before eating.
He wrote a polite letter to thank his aunt.

easy.def: Dirty things that hurt the air, water, or land.
examples: Smoke from cars makes pollution.
Pollution makes the air dirty.
We pick up trash to stop pollution.

more.def: Harmful or dirty things that spoil the air, water, or land.
examples: Pollution in the river made it unsafe for the fish.
Factories must work to cut down on pollution.
Noise pollution from the airport bothers the neighbors.
Soccer is a popular game.
This is a popular book.
Pizza is popular with kids.

more.def: Liked or enjoyed by many people.
examples: That song is so popular that everyone knows the words.
The beach is popular with tourists in summer.
She is popular because she is friendly to everyone.

easy.def: An animal that hunts other animals for food.
examples: A lion is a predator.
A shark is a predator.
The mouse hid from the predator.

more.def: An animal that hunts and eats other animals.
examples: Owls are predators that hunt mice at night.
Wolves are predators that hunt in packs.
Without predators, there would be too many deer.

easy.def: To say what you think will happen.
examples: I predict it will rain today.
Can you predict the end of the story?
I predict we will win.

more.def: To say what you think will happen in the future, using what you already know.
examples: Scientists use clouds and wind to predict the weather.
No one can predict exactly when an earthquake will happen.
The teacher asked us to predict what would float.
We prepare for bed by brushing our teeth.
Dad prepares lunch.
We prepare for the trip.

more.def: To get ready for something, or to make something ready.
examples: The class prepared for the play by practicing every day.
The chef prepared a special meal.
The town prepared for the storm by stacking sandbags.

easy.def: To say you will really do something.
examples: I promise to feed the fish.
Promise you will come back.
She promised to share.

more.def: To tell someone that you will certainly do something.
examples: He promised to return the book by Friday.
The mayor promised to fix the roads.
I promise I will not tell anyone your secret.
A helmet protects your head.
Sunscreen protects your skin.
The dog protects the house.

more.def: To keep someone or something safe from harm.
examples: The mother bird protected her eggs from the cold.
Laws protect rare animals from hunters.
A shell protects the turtle's soft body.

easy.def: Feeling good about something you did.
examples: I am proud of my painting.
Dad is proud of me.
She was proud of her tall tower.

more.def: Feeling pleased about something you or someone else has done.
examples: Her parents were proud when she finished the race.
He is proud to be on the team.
The town is proud of its long history.
